client.value: Atlântico Seguros, a mid-size Portuguese insurer
client.quote: Atlântico Seguros, a mid-size Portuguese insurer

problem_statement.value: Atlântico Seguros wants to understand why property and health claims take too long to settle and what claims operating model it should move to. Motor claims were improved in 2024; property and health were not.
problem_statement.quote: why property and health claims take too long to settle and what claims operating model it should move to

engagement_type.quote: they want a diagnostic and a recommendation, not implementation support

engagement_length.assumption_text: Not given; the Phase Architect estimates the duration.

stakeholders.quote: the COO and the Head of Claims, and the final answer goes to the Board

deliverable_format.value: A written report and a board presentation
deliverable_format.quote: a written report and a board presentation

timeline.value: Recommendations presented to the Board on March 15, 2027

prior_attempts.value: An internal lean program in 2024 cut handling time for motor claims only
prior_attempts.quote: an internal lean program in 2024 that cut handling time for motor claims only

success_criteria.value: Reduce average settlement time for property and health claims; keep customer satisfaction at least at current levels
success_criteria.quote: reduce average settlement time without customer satisfaction dropping

out_of_scope.quote: replacing the claims IT system is out of scope

success_criteria_list: Reduce average settlement time for property and health claims
keep customer satisfaction at least at current levels

market_findings.summary: Supervisor issued new guidance on claims-handling response times for non-life insurers
A peer centralized property claims triage in one hub in 2025
Property damage claims rose after the 2025 storm season

basis.governing_question: Why do property and health claims take too long to settle, and what claims operating model should Atlântico Seguros move to?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Establish why property and health claims take too long to settle and what customers experience along the way.

gate.label: Findings sign-off
gate.decision: Do the findings correctly locate where property and health claims lose time?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Define the claims operating model options for property and health claims and test them against settlement time and satisfaction.

gate.label: Design sign-off
gate.decision: Does the steering group endorse the recommendation to take to the Board?

phases.name: Handover
phases.objective_one_line: Present the findings and recommendations to the COO, Head of Claims and the Board in a written report and presentation.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Are the report and presentation ready to go to the Board of Directors?

workstreams.name: Claims process baseline
workstreams.answers: How do property and health claims flow today, and where does settlement time build up?
activities: Map property and health claims from filing to payment
Analyze operational data on handling and settlement times
Review the 2024 lean program's effect on motor claims

deliverables.name: Settlement-time baseline for property and health claims

workstreams.name: Handler and customer views
workstreams.answers: What do claims handlers and customers experience as causes of delay, and how satisfied are customers today?
activities: Interview claims handlers and managers who do the work
Review customer satisfaction results and complaint records
Interview customers with recent property and health claims

deliverables.name: Customer satisfaction baseline and handler pain points

workstreams.name: Delay drivers and levers
workstreams.answers: Which causes explain the delay in settlement, and which can be changed without replacing the claims IT system?
activities: Test candidate delay causes against claims case files
Size the effect of each cause on settlement time
Separate causes that need replacing the claims IT system

deliverables.name: Ranked causes of delay in claims settlement
Diagnostic readout with improvement areas by claim type

workstreams.name: Target model options
workstreams.answers: Which claims operating models could Atlântico Seguros adopt for property and health claims?
activities: Draft operating model options for property and health claims
Agree option assessment criteria with the steering group

deliverables.name: Claims operating model options with assessment criteria

workstreams.name: Option impact assessment
workstreams.answers: How would each option change settlement time and customer satisfaction for property and health claims?
activities: Model each option's effect on settlement time
Check each option against customer satisfaction measures
Test feasibility with claims handlers and managers

deliverables.name: Option assessment against settlement time and satisfaction

workstreams.name: Recommendation and roadmap
workstreams.answers: Which option best meets the success criteria, and in what sequence would the move happen?
activities: Compare options on the agreed criteria
Sequence the move to the chosen model in steps
Plan the move without replacing the claims IT system

deliverables.name: Transition roadmap for the chosen claims operating model
Recommendation on the claims operating model

workstreams.name: Report and Board materials
workstreams.answers: How will the findings and recommendation be put to the COO, Head of Claims and the Board?
activities: Draft the written report from the engagement findings
Prepare the Board presentation with the sponsors
Confirm the handover with the COO and Head of Claims

deliverables.name: Written report on property and health claims

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Align scope, plan and access to data
events.decision: Does the steering group confirm the scope and the plan of work?
agenda: Present the plan, phases and steering meetings
Align on access to claims data and interviewees
Confirm that replacing the claims IT system is out of scope

events.label: Workshop 1: first findings
events.decision: Which causes of delay should the remaining diagnostic weeks test?
agenda: Present the settlement-time baseline and pain points
Discuss early views on where claims lose time
Confirm the causes to test in the remaining weeks

events.label: Findings sign-off
events.decision: Do the findings correctly locate where property and health claims lose time?
agenda: Present the ranked causes of delay
Review the improvement areas by claim type
Decide whether the diagnostic is signed off

events.label: Workshop 2: model options
events.purpose: Choose options to assess in depth
events.decision: Which operating model options go forward to full assessment?
agenda: Present the claims operating model options
Discuss the options against the assessment criteria
Decide which options to assess in depth

events.label: Design sign-off
events.decision: Does the steering group endorse the recommendation to take to the Board?
agenda: Present the option assessment and the recommendation
Decide whether the recommendation goes to the Board

events.label: Final readout
events.decision: Are the report and presentation ready to go to the Board of Directors?
agenda: Confirm the handover to the Board of Directors

architect_notes: Engagement length is not given; phase lengths are estimates from the archetype's typical weeks (Diagnostic 4-8, Design 6-10) plus 2-3 weeks for Handover.
Only the Board date, March 15, 2027, is given and no start date, so the plan cannot be checked against it.
Not covered by the phases: ASF, supervisor guidance on claims-handling response times. Confirm whether it is in scope.
Handover is added to the archetype's Diagnostic and Design because the final answer goes to the Board; confirm it is wanted.
The brief asks for no implementation; tracking settlement time and satisfaction after the move is not in these phases.
